title: Resident Trust Fund Accounts — Conveyance after Discharge or Death, and Closing
content:
**Clause.** When the resident is discharged or dies, the remaining funds in the Resident Trust Fund Accounts account and a final accounting are conveyed within the conveyance days: on discharge to the resident or legal representative, and after a death to the estate, through the personal representative holding letters from the Register of Wills; a power of attorney gives no authority after death. A resident who stays may withdraw everything and close the account at any time. An account is closed only when its balance is zero.

## Sequence of states on the account

A discharge or death moves an active account into conveyance and issues the final accounting; the account closes after the funds have been conveyed. A resident who stays closes an active account directly.

## Condition read before closing

The account's own record must show a balance of zero before it is closed, whether it closes after conveyance or at the request of a resident who stays.

## Payee by event

| Event | Funds and final accounting go to |
|---|---|
| discharge | the resident or the resident's legal representative |
| death | the estate, through the personal representative holding letters from the Register of Wills |

## Basis Q&A

**After the resident's death, the agent who held power of attorney asks for the remaining balance.** The power of attorney gives no authority after death; the funds go to the estate through the personal representative.

**A resident who is staying wants to close the account but $12.40 remains.** The account closes only once its balance is zero, which the resident may bring about by withdrawing the remainder.
